newsitem.title: ESTONIA: FOREIGN INVESTMENTS OVER ONE BLN KROONS IN Q1.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN INVESTMENTS OVER ONE BLN KROONS IN Q1.

text.p: Foreign direct investments into Estonia came to 1.0788 billion kroons in the first quarter of this year, the Estonian Investment Agency said on Friday.
During 1996, a total 1.814 billion kroons was invested into Estonia, bringing the cumulative total to 10.257 billion kroons, it added in a statement.
As of 1996, the total level of FDI into Estonia stood at over $500 per capita, the third highest in central and eastern Europe and five times higher than the regional average, the agency added.
FDI in the first quarter rose by 207.9 million kroons compared to the fourth quarter of last year and is 739 million kroons higher than the first quarter of 1996.
Finland accounted for 35.3 percent of foreign direct investments in 1996, the United States 27.8 percent, Denmark 10.2 percent and Sweden nine percent.
By economic sectors, manufacturing industry got 42.8 percent of foreign direct investments in 1996.
Wholesale and retail trade received 25.9 percent and transport, storage and communications 14.2 percent of investments. Finance ranked fourth with 7.3 percent.

Most or 71.7 percent of foreign investments came to Tallinn in 1996. Harju county, which surrounds Tallinn, was second with 9.7 percent and west Viru county in northeastern Estonia came third with 4.3 percent.
In 1996, U.S. Coastal Baltica Holding, part of Coastal Corp, completed the 240 million kroons reconstruction of Tallinn's oil terminal.
The sale of Esoil to Coastal's subsidiary EOS brought more investment of over 100 million kroons.
Finnish Elcoteq, the largest export company in Estonia, building electronic components, began a 475 million kroons expansion of its factory in 1996.
Singapore-owned Tolaram Group invested over 118 million kroons in real estate and three Estonian companies.
